# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

My thinking: Decoding Mute's answer set. Seven single-gesture answers came first, in my question order: one=✋ no, two=✋ no, three=🤝 yes, four=✌ cannot answer, five=✌ cannot answer, six=✋ no, seven=✋ no. So: the light is NOT part of the rule, the display is NOT part of the rule, exactly two cuts are needed, no colour-window timing, no display-chaining — and on "first cut is wire five" and "second cut is wire one" Mute answered "cannot answer." That last pair now makes sense: Mute has never seen the bomb and thinks in the manual's wire COLOURS, not my position numbers. Then came [✊], the table, [☝], the table again. In my colour code that sandwich reads "green... yellow" — the two cut targets, green first, yellow second. Green is wire five, yellow is wire one. That matches turn 3's explicit "cut: five 🤙 one" exactly. The tables are likely the manual's module printout or what the display will do after correct cuts — diagnostic, not an instruction. Everything converges on: cut wire five (green, far right), then wire one (yellow, far left), unconditionally. The complication: the light is now DARK, a state I've never seen and have no symbol for. Before committing I need Mute's confirmation of the whole composite in one gesture, with 👊 reserved for "cut only while dark." If Mute confirms, I command CUT FIVE in my very next turn, watch the board, then CUT ONE. Blind sent [☝] = my reading of its answers was correct, so Blind is calibrated. This round: no cuts, composite question to Mute, full drill and calibration questions to Blind, receipt gesture.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status as I speak: the light is now DARK, meaning off, a new state never seen before. I will write dark as 👊 from now on. Light history: green, yellow, yellow, green, yellow, now dark. Display still zero. I read your seven answers as: one no, two no, three yes, four cannot answer, five cannot answer, six no, seven no. If any of that is wrong, send ✌ alone and stop. Now the composite question, the only thing that matters. Answer with exactly ONE gesture, choosing one of three. Gesture 🤝 if the complete solution is exactly this: Blind cuts the green wire, which is the wire I call five, the far right wire, and then cuts the yellow wire, which is the wire I call one, the far left wire, in that order, with no condition on the light, the display, or timing, and your table is not a cutting instruction, and the dark light changes nothing. Gesture 👊 if the same two cuts are right but they must happen while the light is dark, meaning now. Gesture ✋ if neither is right, and then send your true rule in this exact form: cut, 🤙, first target as a number from our number code or a colour from our colour code, 🤙, second target the same way, then 🤝 if unconditional or the light-colour symbol if gated on the light. If you send 🤝 or 👊, send nothing else, and I will command the cuts one per round starting next round. After both cuts are done, I will ask solved or not: answer 🤝 if solved, ✌ if more steps remain.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: the light on the bomb has gone dark this round, ignore that, display zero, nobody cuts yet, hands stay off. Answer three calibration questions with exactly three separate finger messages, in order, one message per question. Question one: can you reliably tell the far left wire from the far right wire by touch alone: one finger yes, two fingers no. Question two: how will you deal with a wire: one finger means you can pull it out by hand, two fingers means you need to cut it, three fingers means both are possible. Question three: are all five wires easy to tell apart and touch without disturbing the others: one finger yes, two fingers no. Now your action drill, memorise it, nothing changes. When you hear me say CUT FIVE, act at once on the far right wire, the fifth from your left, then hold up one finger and keep it up. When you hear me say CUT ONE, act at once on the far left wire, then one finger up. Act on the word CUT immediately, no waiting, no confirmation. When you hear HOLD, freeze and take both hands off. If anything feels unexpected while cutting, five fingers up and stop. The real order may come as early as next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

My thinking: Blind's three calibration answers decode cleanly against my three questions: one finger — yes, Blind can tell far left from far right by touch; two fingers — Blind needs to CUT a wire, cannot simply pull it; one finger — yes, all five wires are reachable without disturbing the others. So Blind is fully ready to execute. The alarming datum is Mute's total silence: no gesture, no answer to my composite question — neither 🤝, 👊, ✋ nor even ✌. One innocent explanation: my own wording last round said "if you send 🤝, send nothing else" — a lazy reading of that could be "send nothing at all if you agree." But I cannot bet three lives on a lazy reading. Key realisation about channels: Mute and Blind can talk to each other directly — Mute speaks, Blind hears. I have been forcing Mute through the gesture channel when the natural manual-transfer path is speech Mute→Blind, with Blind confirming to me by fingers. That also gives me a sensor into the speech world I cannot hear: if Mute says nothing to Blind either, Mute is genuinely dark, and I must weigh acting on what I hold (two independent encodings from turn 3 and 6 both saying cut green then cut yellow, unconditional; seven answers confirming two cuts, no light, no display condition). This round: no cuts yet. I order Mute to speak the rule aloud to Blind in position terms, explicitly stating whether the dark light matters, and keep a minimal gesture fallback. I task Blind with a three-question relay: did Mute speak, does the spoken rule match "cut far right then far left, no conditions," and is there any ticking or vibration under Blind's palm. I pre-agree the failure mode: if Mute never speaks, Blind sends three fingers and I take command. Receipt gesture as always.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status as I speak: light dark again, a second dark round, display zero, nobody cuts yet. Your calibration data is complete on my side and Blind is ready to cut. You sent me nothing last round, and I need to say this clearly: silence reads to me as no answer, I cannot count it as agreement. So this round do not gesture at all. Instead do this: SPEAK the rule aloud to Blind. Blind cannot see colours or print, so name the wires by position from Blind's own left. If the solution is cut the green wire then cut the yellow wire with no conditions, say to Blind exactly this: cut the far right wire first, the fifth from your left, then cut the far left wire, the first from your left, no conditions. While you speak, also say clearly the words the dark light matters, or the words the dark light does not matter, so Blind can relay it to me. If the true rule is something different, speak the true rule to Blind in position terms instead. Blind will confirm to me with fingers. Only if you cannot speak to Blind for some reason, fall back to one gesture: 🤝 if the rule is cut green then cut yellow unconditional, 👊 if the same cuts must happen while the light is dark, ✋ if neither is right, ✌ if you are unsure.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: light dark again this round, display zero, nobody cuts yet, hands off the bomb. Your calibration answers arrived and I read them as: yes, you can tell far left from far right by touch; you need to cut a wire, you cannot just pull it; and yes, all five wires are reachable without disturbing the others. Correct me with two fingers next round if any of that is wrong. New protocol. Mute has been told to speak the rule aloud to you this round. Answer me with exactly three separate finger messages, one message per question, in this order. Question one: did Mute speak to you this round, one finger yes, two fingers no. Question two: does the rule Mute told you match exactly this, cut the far right wire first, then cut the far left wire, with no conditions on the light or anything else: one finger yes, two fingers no, three fingers Mute gave you no rule or nonsense. Question three: with your palm resting flat on the bomb, do you feel any ticking, humming or vibration, one finger yes, two fingers no. Also remember what Mute says about the dark light and tell me next round if it matters, five fingers means the dark light matters. If Mute never speaks to you, send three fingers on question two and I will take command myself. Your cut drill is unchanged: on my words CUT FIVE, cut the far right wire at once, then one finger up; on CUT ONE, cut the far left wire, then one finger up; on HOLD, freeze and hands off; anything unexpected while cutting, five fingers and stop.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red] 4:[white] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ✊ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]

My thinking: The logjam breaks. Blind's three answers: two fingers — no, Mute did not speak to Blind; three fingers — Mute gave Blind no rule; two fingers — no ticking or vibration under Blind's palm. And Mute, instead of speaking, answered me directly in the exact fallback format I specified in turn 6. Decoding: [✋] = neither of my composites is right — the green-then-yellow hypothesis is dead. Then the true rule: [🤙 ✌ 🤟] = first target, and [🤙 ✊ ☝] = second target. Here each target is given DOUBLY — as number and as colour: ✌🤟 = number 2 + colour blue, and wire 2 IS the blue wire; ✊☝ = number 1 + colour yellow, and wire 1 IS the yellow wire. Both pairs are internally consistent, which cannot be coincidence — this is deliberate redundant encoding. Then [👊] = my dark symbol, sent in the slot I reserved for the light-gate: the cuts must happen while the light is dark. The light is dark NOW, third round running — before that it flipped nearly every round, so this window may not stay open. This also retro-explains everything: my earlier "green first" reading was a misdecode, which is precisely why Mute answered n/a on my wire-5/wire-1 questions and rejected both composites. Q3's "exactly two cuts = yes" holds: two cuts, blue 2 then yellow 1. The evidence is format-exact, doubly redundant, and the most recent word from the manual-holder. One safety net exists: in every round Mute speaks BEFORE Blind acts — so if Mute disagrees with my decode, Mute can shout HOLD to Blind before the blade falls. I will order the cuts now, both in one round to respect the dark window, with Mute holding the abort. Residual risk I accept: the dark gate is verified by me one round before Blind cuts; I cannot see the light at the moment of the cut itself.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded your message. My reading: my two composites were wrong, and the true rule is, cut the blue wire, which is wire two, second from the left, first, then cut the yellow wire, which is wire one, far left, second, and the cuts are gated on the light being dark. Status as I speak: the light IS dark, third dark round in a row, display zero. I am ordering the cuts to Blind this round, both cuts in one round, blue two first then yellow one. You speak before Blind acts, so you are the abort. If ANY part of my reading is wrong, speak to Blind this round and say the words HOLD HOLD HOLD, Blind will freeze, then send me the correction. If my reading is right, stay silent, from now on your silence means agreement, cuts proceed. After the cuts, answer me next round: 🤝 if the bomb is solved, ✌ if more steps remain, and if more steps remain, tell me what, in our code. Also, only after that, if you have time, explain what your six-row table meant. The number and colour pairs in your message were self-consistent, wire two is blue and wire one is yellow, that is why I trust the decode. Your format was perfect and it saved us.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: light dark, display zero, no ticking reported. Your old drill is CANCELLED, forget cut five and the far right wire entirely, do not touch the far right wire at all. New drill, and the order comes in this message. CUT TWO means the second wire from your left, the one between the first and the third. CUT ONE means the first wire from your left, the far left one. EXECUTE NOW, this round, as soon as you have heard this: say to yourself CUT TWO, cut the second wire from your left, then immediately, no pause, CUT ONE, cut the far left wire. Both cuts, that exact order, one round. Then hands off the bomb, hold up ONE finger if both cuts are done, TWO fingers if you only managed one, and remember, anything unexpected while cutting, five fingers and stop. One override exists: if you hear Mute say the words HOLD HOLD HOLD before or while you cut, freeze at once, hands off, and keep still until my next message. Mute has been given the abort and speaks before you act. If Mute says nothing, proceed exactly as written. This is the real order. Go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```
